content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (fallback target).**

- **§ 22.4 (p0289)** carries the consent gate and the "not unreasonably withheld" standard (fallback elements 3 and 4 already met verbatim), but the carve-outs are materially asymmetric: M&I "may freely assign" on merger/reorganization/asset sale and to a successor of the M&I Data Services division with no notice, while our only carve-out is a merger where the survivor becomes an Affiliate of a $100MM+ financial institution *and* § 21.11 is complied with. No mutual successor right, no written-notice mechanic — fallback fails.
- **Cure (one surgical replace):** the proviso becomes a mutual, unconditioned right for either party to assign to a successor in a merger, corporate reorganization or sale of substantially all assets on written notice; the untouched opening sentence keeps consent and the reasonableness standard. The § 21.11 cross-reference is dropped from § 22.4 only (§ 21.11 continues to operate on its own terms, so no dangling reference).
- **Not flagged / noted only:** § 21.11(B) (p0284) limits M&I's post-change-of-control obligations to pre-change entities and prior 3-month volumes +25% — a scope limit, not a Vendor termination or re-pricing right, so no walk-away trigger; § 21.11(A) cost allocation is a fees issue; § 11.3 "Following Change in Control of Customer" (p0191) is redacted and unreviewable, and we reserved comment rather than assume it is compliant.
